item.title: Show HN: NSL - WSL for Linux (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
One of the things that Windows really got right is WSL2. I drive an atomic Linux distro for daily use, but wanted a way to develop with multiple different distros with that same WSL UX. NSL is my answer. It is a faithful reproduction of the developer experience, powered by a single VM that hosts one or more systemd-nspawn containers with your development instances. Host file edits and port sharing come along for the ride, just like WSL. Take a look and tell me what you think... It's yet another step in my long journey to keep my host installation free from all the changing and breaking dev dependencies that force a reinstall every few months.

item.title: Show HN: A working 3D model of an Enigma machine (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
I watched the excellent Veritasium video [1] on the Enigma machine, and watched the full animation by Jared Owen [2], but was still a bit confused on how the inner mechanics of an Enigma machine work. I used Astra to build out the inner components through a combination of reference images, writing out hundreds of extremely detailed prompts, and building my own inspection tools to ensure that every part is sized and positioned in a historically accurate way.

It's still a work in progress, but would love any feedback on the experience so far!

1. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JsBZOcqZerk

2. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ybkkiGtJmkM

item.title: Show HN: Jev as the Bletchley Park Analyst: A Software Bombe on Enigma (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
Watched a recent youtube veritasium on the enigma machine and was curious on how JEV would do in regards to the analysts calls made at Bletchley's. I rebuilt the historical sequence into the software ux.

Results were a mixed, which is what made it interesting. Given the right crib, the Bombe breaks 22 of 25 messages; ciphertext-only against 10 plugs, 0 of 25, same wall Bletchley hit. As a judge of "is this decryption German?" Jev is excellent: AUC 0.9999, 159/160 right decisions. As a crib selector it has no skill at all; its ranking is no better than the fixed list.

Against XGBoost an classical judges, it ties on the same kind of data. But trained on synthetic traffic and tested on real intercepts, and XGBoost drops to 53% correc versus zero-shot Jev holds at 97%. Feel free to try it here: https://enigma-jev.vercel.app/ (requires a jev typesafe api key)

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49903792

item.title: Ask HN: How do you handle hitting AI coding agent usage limits? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description:
One topic I've been researching lately is the best way to handle switching to another agent when I hit a usage limit on one of them. For example, if I hit the usage limit on Codex, I would want to switch to Claude Code and vice versa.

The important part is not losing the ongoing context/task(s) when switching between the tools.. I have found a few things that say they do this but none seem to have much traction.

As a result, I was hoping to pick the brain of HN'ers to see how you all handle this

(To head off comments regarding 'pay for a better plan for more usage' - I can't currently really afford the jump from $20 a month per agent to $100-200/m per agent)
